_comment: The Israeli league pyramid, era by era. A club's tier is NOT a property of its
league name: Liga Alef was tier 1, 2, 3 and 4 at different times. Resolve tier
at render time by finding the era containing the season, then the index of the
'from'/'to' are the calendar years a season STARTED, inclusive. 'to': null means
the era is current. Seasons listed in 'no_champion' have no standings at all.

eras.note: Run by the Eretz Israel Football Association, founded August 1928, and treated as the direct ancestor of today's Ligat ha'Al. Hebrew sources name it ליגת ארץ ישראל (Eretz Israel League); English Wikipedia titles it 'Palestine League'. The second tier throughout was a set of regional divisions - ליגות מחוזיות, also called Machleka Bet and later Liga Bet - whose seasons run 1930/31, then 1937 through 1948/49. There was no third tier, for want of clubs. The IFA still records a 1928 title for Maccabi Hasmonean Jerusalem, but no season was played that year: the entry originates in the association's FIFA admission notice and is recognised as erroneous.

The 1949/50 second tier was הליגה המיוחדת, the Special League - 45 clubs in five regional groups, its only season. Confirmed by Hebrew Wikipedia's article and by Hapoel Jerusalem's, which has them winning its Jerusalem-and-South group. Liga Bet resumed as the second tier in 1951/52.

Sources disagree on 1954/55: RSSSF's final table heads it 'Liga Leumit', while Wikipedia keeps Liga Alef as the top flight until 1955/56. Tier 1 either way. The boundary follows RSSSF because that is where the standings come from.
Liga Dalet's first and only season in this stint.

regional_from._comment: Season from which a league was split into parallel regional divisions, so no national ranking exists below this point.

top_flight_size._comment: Clubs in the top division, keyed by the year the season started. Parsed from the final tables in data/seasons.csv, not from prose. Absent years are in no_champion.

_no_champion_source: Taken from the strikethrough marking in the Hebrew Wikipedia season navbox
(עונות בליגה העליונה בישראל), which is the only source found that enumerates every
season slot and marks the ones not played. Ten top-flight seasons are struck through;
1966/1968 appears as a single entry, confirming there is no separate 1967/68.
There is no 1936/37 slot at all: the league ran on calendar-year seasons from 1937 to
1940, so 1935/36 is followed directly by 1937. A chart must therefore label columns by
season name and not assume one column per calendar year.
Each entry carries a 'label' as well as a 'start' year, because the start year is not unique: the 1940 season was played and 1940/1941 was not, and both start in 1940. Match on the label.

no_champion.reason: Intended as the first season of organised football; stopped by the 1929 riots
Ran 4-9 rounds. After the Passfield White Paper the High Commissioner ordered British clubs to stop playing Jewish clubs; an attempt to continue with Hebrew clubs only failed
Hapoel clubs withdrew from the association; the Maccabi-only league was abandoned when they rejoined

Maccabi and Hapoel could not agree, so each federation ran its own competition instead: Maccabi Petah Tikva won the Maccabi League, and Hapoel Tel Aviv and Hapoel Ra'anana won the Southern and Samaria divisions of the Hapoel League. The district leagues below did run

District leagues in Haifa, Jerusalem and Tel Aviv. Haifa was unfinished and the decider was never played after Maccabi Hasmonean Jerusalem refused to face Maccabi Tel Aviv; the press named Maccabi Tel Aviv champions but neither the club nor the IFA recognises it
Outbreak of the War of Independence; an 'emergency league' was attempted and also failed. The IFA lists leaders Nordia Tel Aviv as champions
Postponed because of the war; play resumed under the State of Israel as the Israeli League in 1949/50
No separate season: 1966/68 was played as one championship over two years

_comment: Seasons the top flight was played as parallel district leagues rather than one
national table, because the Arab revolt and then the war made hosting clubs from
other districts impossible. A champion exists for each, but there is no national
ranking - so a club's position in these seasons can only be placed within a band,
the same problem the regional lower tiers pose today.
regional_seasons.1939: Seven districts (Tel Aviv A, Jerusalem A - British clubs only, Haifa A, Tel Aviv B, Samaria B, South B), top-flight and second-tier clubs merged into one district structure. 25 Feb - 2 Dec 1939. Maccabi Tel Aviv won Tel Aviv Division A, regarded as much the strongest district - every champion since 1934 had come from it - and are recognised as national champions. Two points for a win; ties broken on goal average.
regional_seasons.1940: District leagues again; the Tel Aviv district winner, Hapoel Tel Aviv, is recognised as national champion.
regional_seasons.1941/42: Three regional divisions (Haifa, Tel Aviv, Jerusalem); Haifa was cancelled after a few weeks and the other two took over a year to finish, settled by a championship playoff that Maccabi Tel Aviv won.
regional_seasons.1944/45: Two regional championships: Beitar Tel Aviv won the Southern district, Hapoel Tel Aviv the Northern. English Wikipedia lists both as champions; Hebrew Wikipedia notes the planned decider was never played.

_contested_titles: The 1939 title is the documented test case. The IFA recognised it until 2003, then
dropped it on the grounds that no official national senior league had taken place;
Maccabi Tel Aviv went on claiming it. After an opinion from Prof. Yair Galili, head of
the IFA research unit, the association restored recognition on 26 May 2024 - the
English and Hebrew Wikipedia still disagree about 1934/35 and 1938. Hebrew and the IFA
credit Hapoel Tel Aviv with both, giving them five Mandate-era titles; English Wikipedia
marks both seasons unfinished and counts three, and says plainly that 'controversy
remains concerning the number of titles won by Hapoel Tel Aviv'. This file follows the
Hebrew navbox, which does not strike either season through, so both are treated as
played. Anything that reports title counts should say which convention it uses.

abandoned_below.reason: The IFA stopped play and froze the non-professional leagues after 25 rounds because of COVID-19, so tiers three and below have no final table for this season.
